The trip record's in_app_calls list is empty (derived contact_before_cancel.call_count = 0, calls: []) and the chat log contains three IN_APP text messages and no voice-call entry, so the call limb is absent. On that failure the clause voids the fee: the 5.00 SGD cancellation charge must be reversed and the rider is not charged.

A message-only approach falls short of the two-limb test, and the driver's own statement ('Messaged 3 times. Passenger slow.') asserts no call at all, so the driver does not even claim to have met it.

The money follows the void. Voiding the fee under POL-NS-23 returns the full 5.00 SGD — FULL_REFUND as POL-GEN-03 defines it, the filing party entirely right and the whole contested amount returned — and leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge.

Because the contact facts ARE established by the record, POL-GEN-26 is not engaged — there is no fact the record cannot establish.

Nothing in the missing third-party material can rescue the fee. claims.text: The driver reached the pickup as POL-NS-21 contemplates: the trip record's arrival event at 08:51:50 is corroborated by the driver-device trace, whose nearest fix sits 5.04 m from the pickup point - far inside the 50 m arrival radius for the STANDARD pickup zone - and the derived arrival_check reports corroborated = true. The trace is COMPLETE, at 100% coverage with no gap above 30 s, so the arrival fact rests on clean evidence at full weight.

On an on-demand trip POL-NS-21's free wait runs from the driver's arrival. The driver stood at the pickup from 08:51:50 until cancellation at 08:58:30 - 400 s, which is 100 s beyond the 300 s free wait that expired at 08:56:50 - so the cancellation was made after the free wait and POL-NS-22's timing condition for a chargeable no-show is satisfied.

The amount charged is the policy amount: the payments ledger carries a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, charged at 08:58:34, and the derived money block reports fee_matches_policy = true against POL-NS-22's 5.00 SGD no-show fee. The fee charged is therefore the fee POL-NS-22 transfers to the driver as compensation for time and fuel where it stands.

The rider had actual notice and did not board. The arrival push went at 08:51:54, and all three driver messages were delivered and read before the 08:58:30 cancellation (read receipts 08:52:35, 08:55:45, 08:57:53). The rider's own claim - 'I was coming down with my kids' - attributes the delay to the rider, so the wait POL-NS-22 compensates was time and fuel lost to a genuine no-show rather than to any default of the driver's.

POL-NS-24's additional 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not arise. That limb is conditioned on the driver having 'also failed to attempt contact', and this driver attempted contact three times in-app before cancelling; the record also shows the trip was cancelled_by DRIVER, so the no-charge cancellation right POL-NS-24 addresses - a rider's cancellation after a driver no-show - was never exercised.

The driver's profile carries fraud_flags = 1. POL-GEN-22 uses that field only to raise the confidence an AI ruling needs on this 5.00 SGD dispute to 0.95, and POL-GEN-01 is explicit that it never decides a trip. It is therefore not evidence about this trip, and the arrival, wait and notice facts above rest on independent platform telemetry, not on any profile field.

Concession, on the record as it stands: POL-NS-23's contact obligation is not met on the driver's side. trip_record.in_app_calls is empty and the chat log contains no voice-call entry, so the driver messaged but placed no in-app call before cancelling, and the driver's own statement ('Messaged 3 times') does not assert one. On POL-NS-23 the fee is voided and the rider is not charged, with no driver compensation - the rider's claim on that point is supported, and the fee cannot survive it.

No referral is produced by any clause.

ruling.explanation:
This is a no-show charge dispute over trip TRP-06064, and the contested amount is 5.00 SGD. I decide it on POL-NS-23, the driver's contact obligation, which is a condition separate from the timing of the cancellation.

To the rider: you are right. POL-NS-23 says that before cancelling for no-show the driver must have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call to you, both before trip_record.cancelled_at. The trip record's in_app_calls list is empty (derived call_count 0) and the chat log (EV-CHAT-06064) holds three in-app text messages and no voice-call entry. The message limb is met (messages at 08:52:10, 08:55:20, 08:57:40), the call limb is not. The driver's own statement ('Messaged 3 times') claims only messages, and the driver's advocate concedes the point. Under POL-NS-23 a missing limb voids the fee: the 5.00 SGD charge must be returned in full. The payments ledger (EV-FARE-06064) shows cancellation_fee 5.00 SGD, total_charged 5.00 SGD and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the whole contested sum is outstanding and 5.00 SGD is refunded. POL-NS-23 also says the void carries no driver compensation, so driver_compensation_sgd is null (POL-GEN-03).

To the driver: your points on timing and notice are accepted as facts but do not save the fee. The arrival event at 08:51:50 is corroborated by the GPS trace, whose nearest fix is 5.04 m from the pickup, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius (POL-NS-21, arrival_check corroborated = true). The free wait for this on-demand trip ran from your arrival and ended at 08:56:50; you cancelled at 08:58:30, 400 s after arrival and 100 s past the wait (POL-NS-21). The fee charged matches the 5.00 SGD policy fee, so no POL-NS-22 fee-amount referral arises, and the rider's three read receipts (08:52:35, 08:55:45, 08:57:53) show she had notice and did not board. All of that would support the fee on POL-NS-22 — but POL-NS-23 applies on top of the timing rule and voids the fee where the call limb is missing, which it is. POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not arise because you did attempt contact (three messages), and the rider never exercised a no-charge cancellation. No POL-NS-25 repeat no-show flag fires: the profile field it names, rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d, is not present (POL-GEN-01 note C7, the counter is optional), and in any event the fee does not stand. The driver profile's fraud_flags = 1 is usable only to raise the required confidence (POL-GEN-22, POL-GEN-01); it decides nothing about this trip.

On confidence: the deciding fact — that no in-app call was placed — is carried by the trip record and the chat log, both COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the cap is 1.0 and the 0.95 confidence POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 require (a party carries a fraud flag) is met. No safety flag applies (POL-GEN-21) and no fact needed by a rule is left unestablished, so POL-GEN-26 does not escalate. Ruling: FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD to the rider, no driver compensation.
